Baal Cycle — Copenhagen Ugaritic Corpus KTU 1.1-1.6
Cited in the Divine Council Index entry on Genesis 6:1-4.

abel.title: Abel
abel.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
abel.note: Adam and Eve's second son, and a shepherd. God took his offering, the firstborn of the flock, and passed over his brother Cain's, and that is where the first murder comes from. Hebrews says it was the faith behind the offering, not the offering itself.

abel-mizraim.title: Abel-mizraim
abel-mizraim.about: Atad between Jericho and the Jordan(?)
abel-mizraim.note: The name the Canaanites put on the threshing floor of Atad after they watched Joseph and his brothers mourn their father there for seven days. It means mourning of Egypt. Nobody knows where it was.

abida.title: Abida
abida.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abida.note: A son of Midian, which makes him Abraham's grandson through Keturah, the wife he took after Sarah died. The line is counted among the Arab tribes east and south of Canaan.

abimael.title: Abimael
abimael.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abimael.note: Down Joktan's line in the Table of Nations. That family is generally placed in southern Arabia.

abimelech-2.title: Abimelech
abimelech-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
abimelech-2.note: The Philistine king of Gerar. Abraham told him Sarah was his sister and he took her into his household, then gave her back once God warned him in a dream. The same thing played out again later between him and Isaac over Rebekah.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

abram.title: Abram
abram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abram.note: Abraham's name before God changed it, in the covenant of Genesis 17. Same man, earlier chapters.

accad.title: Accad
accad.note: One of the cities Nimrod's kingdom started from, in the Table of Nations. It is named with Babel, Erech and Calneh in the land of Shinar.

achbor-2.title: Achbor
achbor-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
achbor-2.note: A different Achbor entirely, from the time of the patriarchs. Genesis names him only as somebody's father.

adah-2.title: Adah
adah-2.about: Woman living at the time before the Flood
adah-2.note: One of Lamech's two wives, down Cain's line. Genesis names her in three verses together and then leaves her.

adah.title: Adah
adah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
adah.note: One of Esau's wives. She is named through the family lists in Genesis and not outside them.

adam.title: Adam
adam.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
adam.note: The first man. The name is the ordinary Hebrew word for man, which is the point of it.

adbeel.title: Adbeel
adbeel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
adbeel.note: Third of Ishmael's twelve sons. Each of the twelve ended up heading an Arabian tribal confederation.

admah.title: Admah
admah.note: One of the five cities of the plain, always paired with Zeboiim, and destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah.

adullamite.title: Adullamite
adullamite.note: Hirah, Judah's friend in the story of Judah and Tamar, was one. It means a man from Adullam, a Canaanite town in Judah's territory.

aholibamah.title: Aholibamah
aholibamah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
aholibamah.note: She was one of Esau's wives, the daughter of a Hivite chief, and her sons became tribal leaders among the Edomites.

ahuzzath.title: Ahuzzath
ahuzzath.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ahuzzath.note: He came with Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar, when the king made a treaty with Isaac after the disputes over wells.

ai.title: Ai
ai.note: A fortified Canaanite city near Bethel. Israel's first attack was thrown back because of Achan's hidden sin, and once that was dealt with Joshua took the city by ambush. The site is usually identified with et-Tell, though digging there has turned up little from the right period.

aiah-2.title: Aiah
aiah-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
aiah-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

akan.title: Akan
akan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
akan.note: He was Ezer's son and one of the Horite clan chiefs descended from Seir, in the land of Edom before Israel had a king. 1 Chronicles 1:42 spells him Jakan.

aliah.title: Aliah
aliah.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
aliah.note: Another spelling of Alvah, one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau. The two Edomite lists in Genesis and Chronicles differ in small ways like this throughout, and nothing further is recorded of him.

alian.title: Alian
alian.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
alian.note: Also called Alvan. He was a son of Shobal and a Horite clan chief in Seir, and nothing further is known.

allon-bachuth.title: Allon-bachuth
allon-bachuth.note: Oak of weeping. It is the place near Bethel where Rebekah's nurse Deborah was buried, and it was likely the same landmark later called the palm tree of Deborah, where the judge Deborah held court.

almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

almodad.title: Almodad
almodad.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
almodad.note: First of Joktan's sons in the Table of Nations. His descendants are usually put somewhere in the Arabian peninsula, though which tribe has not been settled.

amalek-2.title: Amalek
amalek-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
amalek-2.note: Genesis names him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

amraphel.title: Amraphel
amraphel.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
amraphel.note: King of Shinar, in southern Mesopotamia, and one of the four kings who marched with Chedorlaomer of Elam against Sodom and the cities of the plain. Older scholarship tried to make him Hammurabi, and most scholars now reject the equation.

anah.title: Anah
anah.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
anah.note: He found hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing his father's donkeys, and he sits in the Edomite genealogies of Esau's line.

anamim.title: Anamim
anamim.note: Not a person. The Table of Nations counts them among the groups descended from Mizraim, Egypt, and which real people is meant has not been identified with confidence.

aner.title: Aner
aner.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aner.note: An Amorite chief allied with Mamre and Eshcol, who went with Abraham after the four kings who had captured Lot. 1 Chronicles also gives the name to a Levite town of Kohath's clan in Manasseh.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

aram-3.title: Aram
aram-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram-3.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

aram-naharaim.title: Aram-naharaim
aram-naharaim.note: Aram of the two rivers, upper Mesopotamia. Abraham's relatives settled there, and the wives of Isaac and Jacob came from it.

aran.title: Aran
aran.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
aran.note: A descendant of Seir the Horite, among the clan chiefs of Edom. The Horites were the cave-dwelling people of Mount Seir before the Edomites pushed them out, and lists like this keep their tribal structure. Nothing else about him is recorded.

ararat.title: Ararat
ararat.note: Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat as the floodwaters went down. The region is in what is now eastern Turkey.

ard.title: Ard
ard.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ard.note: Bela's son and Benjamin's grandson, from whom the Ardites came. 1 Chronicles 8:3 calls him Addar.

areli.title: Areli
areli.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
areli.note: He went down to Egypt with Jacob among the seventy, a son of Gad, and his clan, the Arelites, was counted again in the wilderness census.

arioch-2.title: Arioch
arioch-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
arioch-2.note: Genesis names him twice, and he is a king from the patriarchs.

arkite.title: Arkite
arkite.note: Descendants of Canaan who lived at Arka, about twelve miles northeast of Tripoli in modern Lebanon. The site is Tell Arqa, and it appears as Irqata in the Amarna letters.

arodi.title: Arodi
arodi.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
arodi.note: Arod again, under the spelling Genesis uses: Gad's son, founder of the Arodite clan, and one of the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob.

arphaxad.title: Arphaxad
arphaxad.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
arphaxad.note: Shem's son, born two years after the flood. Genesis runs his descendants down through several generations to Abraham, so he is the link between Noah and the patriarchs.

arvadite.title: Arvadite
arvadite.note: The people of Arvad, an island city off the Phoenician coast now called Arwad, descended from Canaan. Assyrian records show it paying tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III and Sennacherib.

asenath.title: Asenath
asenath.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
asenath.note: Pharaoh gave her to Joseph as his wife. She was the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, and she bore him Manasseh and Ephraim, the ancestors of two tribes of Israel.

ashbel.title: Ashbel
ashbel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ashbel.note: Benjamin's son, and his descendants made one of the clans of the tribe.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

ashkenaz.title: Ashkenaz
ashkenaz.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ashkenaz.note: Gomer's son and Japheth's grandson. Jeremiah later calls on a kingdom of Ashkenaz, with Ararat and Minni, to join in the destruction of Babylon.

ashtoreth-karnaim.title: Ashtoreth Karnaim
ashtoreth-karnaim.note: Ashtoreth of the two horns, a city in Bashan east of the Jordan. A branch of the Rephaim lived there until Chedorlaomer's coalition beat them. It is generally identified with Tell Ashtarah in the Golan.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

avith.title: Avith
avith.note: The city of Hadad son of Bedad, one of the early kings of Edom before Israel had kings of its own. He beat the Midianites in the territory of Moab.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal-hanan.title: Baal-hanan
baal-hanan.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
baal-hanan.note: An Edomite king, from the list in Genesis of rulers who reigned before Israel had a king of its own.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

bashemath.title: Bashemath
bashemath.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bashemath.note: One of Esau's wives, in the Genesis lists. The name belongs to more than one of them, and to a daughter of Solomon too.

bashemath-2.title: Bashemath
bashemath-2.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bashemath-2.note: Another of Esau's wives with this name, the one in the Genesis 36 lists.

becher.title: Becher
becher.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
becher.note: Benjamin's son, whose descendants became one of the clans of Benjamin's tribe.

bedad.title: Bedad
bedad.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
bedad.note: Hadad's father. Hadad was one of the early kings of Edom, and he beat the Midianites in the territory of Moab. Nothing else is recorded of Bedad.

beer-lahai-roi.title: Beer-lahai-roi
beer-lahai-roi.note: The well of the one who lives and sees me, in the Negev, where the angel of the Lord found Hagar pregnant and running away and spoke to her. Isaac later settled near it.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

beeri.title: Beeri
beeri.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
beeri.note: Judith's father, a Hittite. She became one of Esau's wives, and the marriage grieved Isaac and Rebekah.

bela-2.title: Bela
bela-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
bela-2.note: An early king, first on the Genesis 36 list, from long before Israel had a throne.

bela.title: Bela
bela.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
bela.note: Two things go by this name in these verses. Bela, also called Zoar, was the one city of the plain spared, kept so Lot had somewhere near to run. The name also belongs to Benjamin's firstborn son.

ben-ammi.title: Ben-ammi
ben-ammi.about: Ammonite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ben-ammi.note: Son of my people. Lot's younger daughter bore him after they fled Sodom, and he became the ancestor of the Ammonites.

ben-oni.title: Ben-oni
ben-oni.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ben-oni.note: Son of my sorrow. Rachel gave the name to her second son as she was dying in childbirth near Bethlehem. Jacob renamed the boy Benjamin, son of the right hand.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beor-2.title: Beor
beor-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
beor-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

bera.title: Bera
bera.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
bera.note: King of Sodom when Chedorlaomer's coalition plundered the cities of the plain and carried off Lot. Abram beat the raiders and got Lot back. Bera came out to meet him and offered him the recovered goods.

bered-2.title: Bered
bered-2.note: A town in the Negev near Beer-lahai-roi, used as a landmark in the story of Hagar running from Sarai.

beriah.title: Beriah
beriah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
beriah.note: A son of Asher, and the head of a clan in the Numbers 26 census. Several other men carry the same name.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bethuel.title: Bethuel
bethuel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
bethuel.note: Nahor and Milcah's son, Abraham's nephew, and the father of Laban and Rebekah. He shows up in person once, to give his consent when Abraham's servant asked for Rebekah as a wife for Isaac.

bilhah.title: Bilhah
bilhah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
bilhah.note: Rachel's maidservant. Laban had given her to Rachel, and when Rachel had no children she gave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife. Bilhah bore him Dan and Naphtali.

bilhan.title: Bilhan
bilhan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
bilhan.note: A Horite clan chief, in Edom's genealogies.

birsha.title: Birsha
birsha.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
birsha.note: King of Gomorrah, one of the five kings who rebelled against Chedorlaomer and lost.

bozrah.title: Bozrah
bozrah.note: Edom's capital, the city of the early Edomite king Jobab. The prophets kept coming back to it in their oracles against Edom. Isaiah pictures the Lord coming from Bozrah in stained garments.

buz-2.title: Buz
buz-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
buz-2.note: It means contempt. This Buz was the second son of Abraham's brother Nahor, and Elihu, one of Job's counsellors, came from his line.

cain.title: Cain
cain.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
cain.note: Adam and Eve's firstborn, a farmer. God accepted his brother Abel's offering and not his, and Cain killed Abel out of jealousy. God marked him and sent him off to wander rather than putting him to death.

cainan.title: Cainan
cainan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
cainan.note: Two men in the genealogies. One descends from Seth several generations before Noah; the other is a son of Arphaxad in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, a name missing from the Genesis Hebrew text but present in the Greek.

calah.title: Calah
calah.note: Nimrod is said to have built it in Assyria, along with Nineveh and Resen, and it is identified with Nimrud on the east bank of the Tigris south of Mosul.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaan-2.title: Canaan
canaan-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
canaan-2.note: The person, not the land. In Genesis 9 he is the son on whom the curse falls, and the people of the land would trace back to him.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

carmi.title: Carmi
carmi.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
carmi.note: Reuben's son, whose family became one of the tribe's clans.

casluhim.title: Casluhim
casluhim.note: A people, not a person. They descend from Mizraim, the ancestor of Egypt, in the Table of Nations, and Genesis says the Philistines came from them.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

chedorlaomer.title: Chedorlaomer
chedorlaomer.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
chedorlaomer.note: An Elamite king. His coalition raided Sodom and carried off Lot along with the city's goods. Abraham got everything back in a surprise night attack.

cheran.title: Cheran
cheran.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
cheran.note: Dishon's son, from the Horite clans of Seir. The Horites lived in the region before Edom's kings arose and were later pushed out or absorbed.

chesed.title: Chesed
chesed.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
chesed.note: Nahor's son, one of the descendants of Abraham's brother listed in Genesis 22:22. Some scholars connect the name with the Hebrew word for the Chaldeans, Kasdim.

chezib.title: Chezib
chezib.note: The town where Shelah, Judah's third son by his Canaanite wife, was born, generally taken as another name for Achzib in the Shephelah, though nobody has found the site.

chittim-2.title: Chittim
chittim-2.note: Named twice, in Genesis and 1 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

chush-2.title: Chush
chush-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
chush-2.note: Ham's eldest son, whose descendants are tied to the country south of Egypt that carries his name.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

dan-2.title: Dan
dan-2.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
dan-2.note: Jacob's son by Bilhah, Rachel's servant, and the ancestor of the tribe that carries his name.

deborah-2.title: Deborah
deborah-2.about: Prophetess living at the time of the Patriarchs
deborah-2.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

dedan-2.title: Dedan
dedan-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
dedan-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

dedan-3.title: Dedan
dedan-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
dedan-3.note: One of 3 men called Dedan. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

diklah.title: Diklah
diklah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
diklah.note: A son of Joktan in the table of nations, more likely a tribal territory than one man. The name means palm grove, which points to a date-growing district of Arabia, but where is uncertain.

dinah.title: Dinah
dinah.about: Jacob's daughter living at the time of the Patriarchs
dinah.note: Jacob and Leah's only daughter. After Shechem raped her, Simeon and Levi made the men of his city agree to be circumcised and then killed them all while they were still recovering. On his deathbed Jacob condemned it as reckless cruelty.

dinhaban.title: Dinhaban
dinhaban.note: A place, not a person, and a variant spelling of Dinhabah, the capital of Bela son of Beor, first on Edom's list of early kings. It lay somewhere south and east of the Dead Sea; the site is unknown.

dishan.title: Dishan
dishan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
dishan.note: Youngest of the sons of Seir, a Horite chief among Edom's earlier people.

dishon.title: Dishon
dishon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
dishon.note: One of the Horite chiefs who held Edom's land before Esau's descendants settled it.

dishon-2.title: Dishon
dishon-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
dishon-2.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

dodanim.title: Dodanim
dodanim.note: A seafaring people descended from Javan, not a single man. Chronicles spells the name Rodanim, which many connect to Rhodes or to the Dardanians of northwest Asia Minor.

dumah.title: Dumah
dumah.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
dumah.note: A son of Ishmael, and the Arabian tribe and region that came from him, usually tied to the oasis of Dumat al-Jandal.

ebal.title: Ebal
ebal.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ebal.note: The mountain of the curses, opposite Mount Gerizim near Shechem. Moses ordered six tribes onto Ebal to speak the covenant's curses while six on Gerizim spoke its blessings, and Joshua built an altar there and wrote the law on stones. A Horite chief descended from Seir carried the name too.

eber.title: Eber
eber.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eber.note: Several generations before Abraham in Shem's line, and his name is the likely source of the word Hebrew.

eden.title: Eden
eden.note: The garden where God put the first humans. A river ran out of it and split into four, the Tigris and the Euphrates among them, which is why most people look for it in the lowlands of ancient Mesopotamia. Its exact site cannot be fixed.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

egypt-3.title: Egypt
egypt-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
egypt-3.note: In Genesis 10 and 1 Chronicles 1 Egypt is a person, one of the fathers in the list of nations.

ehi.title: Ehi
ehi.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ehi.note: One of Benjamin's sons who went down to Egypt with Jacob. The other lists spell the family Ahiram or Aharah, which is common in these tribal rolls.

el-paran.title: El-paran
el-paran.note: The oak or terebinth of Paran, on the edge of the wilderness by the Horites in Seir. The kings under Chedorlaomer got this far before they turned back toward the Dead Sea cities.

elah-3.title: Elah
elah-3.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
elah-3.note: One of 5 men called Elah. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

elam.title: Elam
elam.note: A kingdom east of Babylon. In the prophets it is one of the nations among which God scattered Israel. Its people turn up again at Pentecost.

elam-3.title: Elam
elam-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
elam-3.note: One of 7 men called Elam. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

eldaah.title: Eldaah
eldaah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eldaah.note: Youngest of Midian's sons, Abraham's grandson through Keturah, and ancestor of one of the Arabian groups that came from Midian.

eliezer-10.title: Eliezer
eliezer-10.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eliezer-10.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

eliphaz.title: Eliphaz
eliphaz.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
eliphaz.note: Esau's son, the first of the Edomite line in Genesis 36, and father of a string of Edomite chiefs.

elishah.title: Elishah
elishah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
elishah.note: A son of Javan, whose descendants Ezekiel ties to the fine purple dye that Tyre bought.

ellasar.title: Ellasar
ellasar.note: A kingdom, not a person. Arioch ruled it and marched with Chedorlaomer against Sodom. Many connect it with Larsa, between Ur and Uruk, a city that has been well excavated.

elon.title: Elon
elon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
elon.note: A Hittite whose daughter Basemath married Esau; the name means oak.

elon-2.title: Elon
elon-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
elon-2.note: Genesis and Numbers name him twice, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

emims.title: Emims
emims.note: A people of unusual height who lived in Moab's land before they were pushed out, remembered in Deuteronomy alongside the Anakim.

en-mishpat.title: En-mishpat
en-mishpat.note: Spring of judgment, the old name for Kadesh in the wilderness south of Canaan. Chedorlaomer's kings hit it on the campaign that ended with Abram chasing them to get Lot back.

enaim.title: Enaim
enaim.note: Tamar sat veiled at Enaim and waited for Judah, who had not given her his youngest son. The name means two springs, or two eyes, and the spot is usually placed between Adullam and Timnah.

enoch.title: Enoch
enoch.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
enoch.note: Seventh from Adam. Genesis says he walked with God, and then he was not, for God took him, with no death notice like the others. Jude quotes a prophecy in his name, and a whole later body of Jewish apocalyptic writing carries it too, though written centuries after him.

enoch-2.title: Enoch
enoch-2.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
enoch-2.note: Named twice, in Genesis, and nowhere else.

enos.title: Enos
enos.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
enos.note: Seth's son. In his days, Genesis says, people began to call on the name of the Lord.

ephah.title: Ephah
ephah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephah.note: Midian's son and Abraham's grandson through Keturah. His people settled in northern Arabia, and Isaiah pictures the land of Ephah bringing gold and incense to Zion.

epher.title: Epher
epher.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
epher.note: A son of Midian, named in the two lists of Midian's sons and nowhere else.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ephron.title: Ephron
ephron.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephron.note: The Hittite who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It was the first piece of the promised land Abraham owned, and Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and their wives were all buried there.

er.title: Er
er.note: Judah's firstborn. Genesis says only that he was wicked in the Lord's sight and God put him to death, and his widow Tamar's story starts from there.

erech.title: Erech
erech.note: Nimrod's kingdom took in Erech, with Babel and Akkad, in the plain of Shinar. It is Uruk, modern Warka in Iraq, among the oldest cities anywhere and probably where cuneiform writing began.

eri.title: Eri
eri.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eri.note: A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. His descendants were the Erites of the wilderness census.

esau.title: Esau
esau.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau.note: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, born red and hairy just ahead of Jacob. He sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, and Jacob later tricked him out of the blessing too, and only after years apart did the two make up in tears. His descendants were the Edomites.

esau-2.title: Esau
esau-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau-2.note: A man from the patriarchs. Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him 7 times.

esek.title: Esek
esek.note: A well, not a person. Isaac's herdsmen dug it in the valley of Gerar and the herdsmen of Gerar claimed the water, so he called it contention. Sitnah came next, and then Rehoboth, which nobody fought over.

eshban.title: Eshban
eshban.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
eshban.note: One of Dishon's four sons, a Horite among the clan chiefs of Seir.

eshcol.title: Eshcol
eshcol.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eshcol.note: An Amorite ally who helped Abraham get Lot back from Chedorlaomer. The Valley of Eshcol near Hebron, probably named for him or his clan, is where the twelve spies cut the huge cluster of grapes.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

eve.title: Eve
eve.about: Woman living at the time before the Flood
eve.note: The first woman, made from Adam's rib as a fit companion, and named the mother of all the living. The serpent deceived her into eating from the one forbidden tree, and Adam ate too. Paul later sets that against the obedience of Christ.

ezbon-2.title: Ezbon
ezbon-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ezbon-2.note: A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. Numbers calls him Ozni.

ezer.title: Ezer
ezer.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ezer.note: A chieftain of Seir, named in Edom's early lists of clan heads.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gaham.title: Gaham
gaham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
gaham.note: One of the sons Nahor, Abraham's brother, had by his concubine Reumah. Nothing further is recorded.

galeed.title: Galeed
galeed.note: Not a person but a heap of stones. Jacob and Laban piled it up to seal their covenant. Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha in Aramaic, and Jacob's Hebrew name for it means heap of witness.

gatam.title: Gatam
gatam.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
gatam.note: Esau's grandson through Eliphaz, and one of the chiefs of Edom, the dukes of the old translations, heading a clan and otherwise only a name in the lists.

gera-2.title: Gera
gera-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
gera-2.note: The name ran in the Benjamite tribe. This Gera is in Genesis 46:21 and in 1 Chronicles 8:5, and Judges 3:15 makes a Gera the father of Ehud, the left-handed judge.

gerar.title: Gerar
gerar.note: Abraham and Isaac both stayed in this Philistine town in the Negev under a king called Abimelech, and both passed their wives off as sisters out of fear. Isaac reaped a hundredfold there and dug out his father's wells again until quarrels over water moved him on toward Beersheba. Tel Haror is a leading candidate for the site.

gershom.title: Gershom
gershom.note: These verses are the census ones, Genesis 46:11, Exodus 6:16 and Numbers 3 and 4, where his family is counted and given its share of the tabernacle work. The note filed with them describes Moses's firstborn, born in Midian and named for a stranger there, who is a different man.

gether.title: Gether
gether.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
gether.note: A son of Aram in Genesis 10:23, most likely standing for an Aramean clan rather than one ancestor, and no later trace of it has been found.

gihon.title: Gihon
gihon.note: Two waters carry the name. One is a river out of Eden that circles Cush and has never been matched to a known river. The other is Jerusalem's only natural spring, in the Kidron Valley, which Hezekiah ran underground into the city before Sennacherib's siege, and the tunnel can still be walked.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

girgashite.title: Girgashite
girgashite.note: Descended from Canaan in Genesis 10, and one of the peoples on the list Israel was to drive out. Where exactly they lived is unclear, though they are generally placed in the central hill country.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

gomer.title: Gomer
gomer.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
gomer.note: Genesis 10 makes him a son of Japheth, and the name stands for his descendants too, which is how Ezekiel 38:6 can list Gomer as a nation. Hosea's wife has the same name and is a different person.

gomorrah.title: Gomorrah
gomorrah.note: Destroyed with Sodom for its wickedness, and the two became shorthand for a people ripe for judgment, from Moses through Jesus and the apostles. No remains have been confirmed. It is generally placed near the southern basin of the Dead Sea.

goshen.title: Goshen
goshen.note: Joseph settled Jacob and the family here, in the eastern Nile delta, and Israel lived and multiplied there until the exodus. Pithom and Rameses were inside it, and it is generally identified with the Wadi Tumilat.

guni.title: Guni
guni.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
guni.note: One of Naphtali's sons, and a clan of the tribe came from him.

hadad-3.title: Hadad
hadad-3.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
hadad-3.note: A son of Ishmael, in the list of Genesis 25:15. Nothing else is told of him.

hadad-2.title: Hadad
hadad-2.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
hadad-2.note: One of the kings of Edom, in Genesis 36 and the matching list in Chronicles. The name was common among them.

hadar.title: Hadar
hadar.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
hadar.note: The last of the Edomite kings listed before Israel had a king. He ruled from Pau and his wife was Mehetabel. Chronicles calls him Hadad, so Hadar may only be a copying variant.

hadoram.title: Hadoram
hadoram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hadoram.note: Genesis 10:27 makes him one of Joktan's sons. Under the same name Chronicles has a prince sent to congratulate David on a victory, and the official over Solomon's forced labour who was stoned to death when the kingdom split under Rehoboam.

hagar.title: Hagar
hagar.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
hagar.note: Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham to have the child Sarah could not, and she bore Ishmael. After Isaac came, Sarah had her and the boy sent into the wilderness, and God met her there. She is the only person in Genesis who gives God a name of her own, the God who sees me.

haggi.title: Haggi
haggi.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
haggi.note: Gad's second son, one of the seventy who went down into Egypt. The Haggite clan in the wilderness census came from him, and nothing else is recorded.

ham-2.title: Ham
ham-2.note: The eastern kings under Chedorlaomer beat the Zuzim here, on the campaign that ended with Lot captured at Sodom. If the Zuzim are the Zamzummim, Ham lay east of the Jordan in what became Ammon. It has nothing to do with Noah's son.

ham.title: Ham
ham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ham.note: Noah's son. He saw his father drunk and naked in the tent and told his brothers instead of covering him, and when Noah woke he cursed Ham's son Canaan, not Ham. Egypt and Cush are among the peoples Genesis 10 traces to him.

hamathite.title: Hamathite
hamathite.note: The people of Hamath, counted among Canaan's descendants. Their city on the Orontes kept marking Israel's northern border, and Assyrian records put its king Irhuleni beside Ahab against Shalmaneser III at Qarqar in 853 BC.

hamor.title: Hamor
hamor.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hamor.note: The Canaanite ruler of Shechem. His son raped Dinah, and while Hamor tried to arrange a marriage, Simeon and Levi talked the men of the city into circumcision and killed them while they were still in pain.

hamul.title: Hamul
hamul.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hamul.note: Perez's son and Judah's grandson. One of Judah's clans came from him.

haran.title: Haran
haran.note: Abraham's family stopped and settled here for a while on the way toward Canaan, and Abraham set out again from Haran in Genesis 12:4. The city was likely named after his brother.

haran-2.title: Haran
haran-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
haran-2.note: Abraham's brother and Lot's father, who died young in Ur before the family moved.

havilah-3.title: Havilah
havilah-3.note: Genesis puts it near the rivers of Eden and calls it rich in gold. The name turns up in two different family lines, so it may be two places.

havilah-4.title: Havilah
havilah-4.note: Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.

havilah.title: Havilah
havilah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
havilah.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

havilah-2.title: Havilah
havilah-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
havilah-2.note: Cush's son in Genesis 10:7. The same name is also a land rich in gold by Eden's rivers, and a son of Joktan, so it may cover more than one region.

hazarmaveth.title: Hazarmaveth
hazarmaveth.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hazarmaveth.note: Joktan's son, in the Arabian branch of Shem's descendants. The name survives almost unchanged in Hadramawt, a region of southern Arabia in Yemen known in the ancient world for frankincense and spice.

hazezon-tamar.title: Hazezon-tamar
hazezon-tamar.note: An Amorite town by the Dead Sea that Chedorlaomer's kings attacked in Abraham's day, later called En-gedi. The old name comes back in Jehoshaphat's reign, when Moabites, Ammonites and Meunites come up against Judah from there.

hazo.title: Hazo
hazo.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hazo.note: Nahor and Milcah had him, one of the sons who became Aramean clans. Nahor was Abraham's brother.

heber.title: Heber
heber.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
heber.note: Not the Kenite. This Heber is in Genesis 46:17 among the family that went down to Egypt, and Numbers 26:45 makes him the head of a clan.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

hemam.title: Hemam
hemam.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
hemam.note: Lotan's son and grandson of Seir the Horite, among the clan chiefs, and 1 Chronicles 1:39 calls him Homam.

hemdan.title: Hemdan
hemdan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
hemdan.note: Eldest son of Dishon, one of the Horite chiefs who held the land before Esau's descendants took it. Chronicles calls him Hamran.

heth.title: Heth
heth.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
heth.note: Canaan's son and the father of the Hittites, the people Abraham bought Sarah's burial cave from and the people Uriah, Bathsheba's husband, came from generations later.

hezron.title: Hezron
hezron.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hezron.note: Perez's son, and the line that ends in David runs through him; Ruth closes with it and Matthew picks it up. The same name marks a spot on Judah's southern border, west of Kadesh-barnea.

hezron-2.title: Hezron
hezron-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hezron-2.note: Reuben's son, listed with the family that went down to Egypt and again in Reuben's line in Exodus and Chronicles. He is a different man from Perez's son of the same name.

hiddekel.title: Hiddekel
hiddekel.note: The Tigris, under its Hebrew name. It is one of the four rivers out of Eden, running east of Assyria, and Daniel is standing on its bank when his last vision comes.

hirah.title: Hirah
hirah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hirah.note: Judah's friend from Adullam. He was there when Judah married a Canaanite woman. Later Judah sent him with a goat to pay the woman he had slept with, who was Tamar in disguise.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

hobah.title: Hobah
hobah.note: North of Damascus. It marks how far Abram chased the four kings who had taken Lot, after routing them at night near Dan. Nobody has matched it to a modern site.

hori.title: Hori
hori.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
hori.note: In Edom's genealogies he is one of the Horite clan chiefs, and that is all the record gives.

horims.title: Horims
horims.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
horims.note: They lived in the region that became Edom before Esau's descendants pushed them out. Genesis records them as the land's earlier people.

hul.title: Hul
hul.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hul.note: Aram's son, Shem's grandson, in the Table of Nations. Like the other names there it probably means a clan or district. Its location is not known.

huppim-2.title: Huppim
huppim-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
huppim-2.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

husham.title: Husham
husham.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
husham.note: He was king of Edom in the days before Israel had any king.

hushim-3.title: Hushim
hushim-3.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hushim-3.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

imna.title: Imna
imna.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
imna.note: A son of Asher. Genesis, Numbers and Chronicles all list him. Numbers counts a clan from him.

irad.title: Irad
irad.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
irad.note: Cain's grandson through Enoch and Mehujael's father. His line runs on to Lamech and the culture-founders Jabal, Jubal and Tubal-cain.

iram.title: Iram
iram.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
iram.note: A clan chief of Edom, from Esau's descendants in the hill country of Seir.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

iscah.title: Iscah
iscah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
iscah.note: Haran's daughter, sister to Milcah and Lot, in one line of Terah's family record. Jewish tradition sometimes made her Sarah, though Genesis never says so.

ishbak.title: Ishbak
ishbak.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishbak.note: Abraham had him by Keturah. He is usually taken as the ancestor of an Arabian tribe, but nobody can say which.

ishmael-2.title: Ishmael
ishmael-2.about: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishmael-2.note: Abraham's first son, by Hagar, Sarah's servant. Sarah had given Hagar to Abraham while she was still childless, then wanted mother and son gone after Isaac came. God promised Hagar her son would father a great nation too, though the covenant line ran through Isaac.

ishmaelite.title: Ishmaelite
ishmaelite.about: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishmaelite.note: The Ishmaelites came from Abraham's son Ishmael and traded across the country south and east of Canaan. One of their caravans bought Joseph from his brothers and took him down to Egypt.

ishuai.title: Ishuai
ishuai.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ishuai.note: One of the household that went down to Egypt, named again in the Numbers census with a clan of his own and once more in Chronicles.

ishvah.title: Ishvah
ishvah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ishvah.note: A son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family. Numbers leaves him out of Asher's clans, which may mean he founded no line.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

ithran.title: Ithran
ithran.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ithran.note: A Horite clan name, from Edom's earlier inhabitants.

jabal.title: Jabal
jabal.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
jabal.note: Cain's line through Lamech and Adah comes down to him and his brother: Jabal is "the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle", and Jubal is credited with music.

jabbok.title: Jabbok
jabbok.note: Jacob crossed this stream alone the night before he met Esau, wrestled until daybreak, and came away named Israel and limping. It runs west into the Jordan through a gorge in Gilead, halfway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, and is the Zarqa River today.

jachin.title: Jachin
jachin.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jachin.note: One of the men who went down to Egypt, and a clan is counted from him in the Numbers census. The same name, meaning "he shall establish", was given to one of the temple's two bronze pillars.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jahleel.title: Jahleel
jahleel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jahleel.note: Zebulun's third son, and the Jahleelite clan came from him.

jahzeel.title: Jahzeel
jahzeel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jahzeel.note: The first of Naphtali's four sons, who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household. The Jahzeelites came from him, and nothing else is recorded of him.

jalam.title: Jalam
jalam.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jalam.note: Esau's son by Oholibamah, whose descendants became one of Edom's clans.

jamin.title: Jamin
jamin.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jamin.note: One of Simeon's sons, in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers and Chronicles. The name was common.

japheth.title: Japheth
japheth.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
japheth.note: Noah's son. With Shem he covered their drunken father without looking, and Noah asked God to enlarge Japheth's territory. Genesis 10 traces his descendants to the peoples of Asia Minor and the Aegean.

jared.title: Jared
jared.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
jared.note: Enoch's father, in Seth's line down to Noah, and he lived nine hundred sixty-two years.

javan.title: Javan
javan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
javan.note: Japheth's fourth son in the table of nations. The Hebrews took his descendants to be the Ionians, the Greek world, and the prophets use Javan to mean Greece and its merchants. Modern Hebrew still calls Greece by the name.

jegar-sahadutha.title: Jegar-Sahadutha
jegar-sahadutha.note: Laban's Aramaic name for the heap of stones he and Jacob raised in Gilead to witness their covenant. Jacob called it Galeed. Both names mean "heap of witness".

jehush.title: Jehush
jehush.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jehush.note: Esau's son, more often spelled Jeush. Several other men in Chronicles carry the name.

jemuel.title: Jemuel
jemuel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jemuel.note: He was Simeon's eldest son and one of the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family, and the later census of Simeon's clans calls him Nemuel.

jerah.title: Jerah
jerah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jerah.note: His name means "moon" in Hebrew. He was a son of Joktan, in Shem's line. An Arabian tribe came from him. Little else is known about it.

jetheth.title: Jetheth
jetheth.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetheth.note: Edom had clan chiefs who came down from Esau, and Jetheth is listed with them.

jetur.title: Jetur
jetur.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
jetur.note: He was Ishmael's son, and Chronicles records a war in which Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh beat his descendants.

jezer.title: Jezer
jezer.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jezer.note: He was Naphtali's son. His family became one of Naphtali's clans.

jidlaph.title: Jidlaph
jidlaph.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jidlaph.note: He was Nahor's son by Milcah, and Nahor was Abraham's brother. Jidlaph is one name in the list of his children and nothing more.

job-2.title: Job
job-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
job-2.note: One of the seventy who went down to Egypt, a son of Issachar. He shares the name with the man in the book of Job only in most English versions. Numbers and Chronicles call him Jashub.

jobab.title: Jobab
jobab.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
jobab.note: An early king of Edom, from the list in Genesis 36 of kings who ruled there before Israel had any.

jobab-2.title: Jobab
jobab-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jobab-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

jokshan.title: Jokshan
jokshan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jokshan.note: He was Abraham's son by Keturah, and Sheba and Dedan, names tied to Arabian trading peoples, came from him.

joktan.title: Joktan
joktan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
joktan.note: The father of a long list of Arabian peoples in Genesis, and Eber's son. His brother Peleg's line is the one that leads to Abraham.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

jubal.title: Jubal
jubal.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
jubal.note: Lamech and Adah's son, in Cain's line, and father of everyone who plays the lyre and pipe. He is the first musician the Bible names.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

judith.title: Judith
judith.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
judith.note: Beeri the Hittite's daughter, one of two Hittite wives Esau took at forty, and the marriage grieved Isaac and Rebekah. She is usually matched with Oholibamah in the later list in Genesis 36, but the two lists name the wives differently and the match has long been argued over.

kadesh.title: Kadesh
kadesh.note: Kadesh-barnea, Israel's main camp in the wilderness of Zin. Moses sent the twelve spies from there, Miriam died there, and there he struck the rock and lost his way into Canaan. It is usually identified with Ain el-Qudeis or Ain el-Qudeirat, where a fortress of the Israelite period has been dug up.

kadmonites.title: Kadmonites
kadmonites.note: "Easterners." God named them among the peoples in the land when he promised it to Abram. They never turn up again, and nobody knows who they were.

kedar.title: Kedar
kedar.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedar.note: Ishmael's son, and the father of a desert tribe known for dark tents and good archers. Poets use Kedar for far-off wilderness living, and the Song of Solomon uses it for dark beauty.

kedemah.title: Kedemah
kedemah.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedemah.note: He was the youngest of Ishmael's twelve sons, and his name means "eastward," which suits sons who settled east of Canaan. Nothing else is recorded about him individually.

kemuel-2.title: Kemuel
kemuel-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
kemuel-2.note: Nahor's son, and so Abraham's nephew.

kenaz.title: Kenaz
kenaz.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
kenaz.note: One of Edom's clan chiefs, in Genesis 36 and again in Chronicles. The Kenizzites are counted among the Edomite clans.

kenezite-2.title: Kenezite
kenezite-2.note: Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.

kenite.title: Kenite
kenite.note: They were a wandering clan close to Midian, outside the twelve tribes but mostly friendly to Israel. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, was a Kenite priest, and Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, killed Sisera.

keturah.title: Keturah
keturah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
keturah.note: The wife Abraham took after Sarah died. Her six sons became Arabian and Midianite peoples, and Abraham sent them away with gifts so Isaac would stand alone as heir.

kiriathaim.title: Kiriathaim
kiriathaim.note: It started out as a town of Reuben's and ended up in Moab, on Jeremiah's list of the cities God's judgment would fall on.

kirjath-arba.title: Kirjath-arba
kirjath-arba.note: "Arba's city," Hebron's older name, after a great man among the Anakim. Sarah died there and Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah close by to bury her. Joshua gave it to Caleb for the faithful report he brought back as a spy.

kohath.title: Kohath
kohath.about: Levi's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kohath.note: Levi's second son. His descendants had the holiest work in the tabernacle, carrying the ark and the sacred furniture on poles, and even they would die if they touched those things.

korah-2.title: Korah
korah-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
korah-2.note: An Edomite chief in Genesis 36 and Chronicles, with nothing to do with the Levite who rebelled.

korah-4.title: Korah
korah-4.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
korah-4.note: One of 4 men called Korah. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named once in Genesis.

laban.title: Laban
laban.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
laban.note: Rebekah's brother and Jacob's uncle, and then his father-in-law twice, after he slipped Leah in where Rachel should have been and got fourteen years of work out of him. He kept changing Jacob's wages as the flocks grew. Jacob finally slipped away with his family, and the two parted under a covenant, not with a fight.

lamech.title: Lamech
lamech.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
lamech.note: Noah's father, from Seth's line. He named his son Noah in the hope that the boy would bring relief from farming the cursed ground. Luke's genealogy keeps him as one link in the chain.

lamech-2.title: Lamech
lamech-2.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
lamech-2.note: He was Cain's descendant. He boasted to his two wives that he had killed a young man just for wounding him. Cain's violence came down to him and got worse.

lasha.title: Lasha
lasha.note: The eastern corner of Canaan in the Table of Nations, with Sidon at the north. Jewish tradition put it at Callirhoe, the hot springs on the east shore of the Dead Sea where Herod the Great is said to have gone in his last illness.

leah.title: Leah
leah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
leah.note: Jacob's first wife, given to him by her father Laban in place of Rachel, and Jacob only found out in the morning. He never loved her the way he loved Rachel. Genesis says God gave her children because she was unloved, and she bore six of the twelve sons, Judah among them.

lehabim.title: Lehabim
lehabim.note: A people descended from Mizraim, the ancestor of Egypt, in the Table of Nations. The name is widely tied to the Lebu of Egyptian inscriptions, ancestors of the Libyans on the coast west of Egypt.

letushim.title: Letushim
letushim.note: A tribe, not a person. They were one of three groups from Dedan, Abraham's grandson through Keturah, with Asshurim and Leummim, and who they were in history is uncertain.

leummim.title: Leummim
leummim.note: The word means "peoples." It names a group of Arabian tribes from Dedan, Abraham's grandson through Keturah, listed with Asshurim and Letushim.

levi.title: Levi
levi.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levi.note: Jacob's third son. He and Simeon massacred the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped, and Jacob cursed them both for it on his deathbed. Even so, Levi's descendants became Israel's priestly tribe, given service at the tabernacle instead of land, partly for their zeal against the golden calf at Sinai.

lot.title: Lot
lot.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
lot.note: Abraham's nephew, who came with him from Ur. When their herdsmen started fighting and they split, Lot took the green Jordan valley and ended up living by Sodom. Angels dragged him out before it burned, and his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt. Afterwards his two daughters got him drunk and had sons by him, the fathers of Moab and Ammon.

lotan.title: Lotan
lotan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
lotan.note: He was a Horite chief whose sister Timna made him Esau's brother-in-law, and his people were living in Edom's land before Edom.

lud.title: Lud
lud.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
lud.note: Shem's son. His people are usually taken to be the Lydians of Asia Minor. Some later passages may mean a people in Africa instead.

luz.title: Luz
luz.note: It was the old Canaanite name of Bethel, where Jacob dreamed of the stairway to heaven, and it hung on in a nearby town after Bethel was renamed.

maachah-9.title: Maachah
maachah-9.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
maachah-9.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

machir.title: Machir
machir.about: Manasseh's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
machir.note: Manasseh's son. His clan, the Machirites, were such fighters that Machir's name can stand for the whole half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.

machpelah.title: Machpelah
machpelah.note: The cave near Hebron that Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite, with its field, to bury his family. Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah all ended up there. Herod's massive stone enclosure still stands over the traditional site, now a mosque and a synagogue.

madai.title: Madai
madai.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
madai.note: Japheth's son, and the ancestor of the Medes, who later joined Persia in taking Babylon.

magdiel.title: Magdiel
magdiel.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
magdiel.note: One of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau, in the lists at Genesis 36:43 and 1 Chronicles 1:54. The name may mark a clan territory more than a single ruler.

magog-2.title: Magog
magog-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
magog-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

mahalaleel.title: Mahalaleel
mahalaleel.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
mahalaleel.note: Seth's line, on the way down to Noah, four generations before Enoch.

mahalath-3.title: Mahalath
mahalath-3.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
mahalath-3.note: Ishmael's daughter, and the wife Esau took to please his parents after his Canaanite wives had upset them. Genesis seems to call her Bashemath as well.

mahanaim.title: Mahanaim
mahanaim.note: "Two camps." Jacob met the angels of God here near the Jabbok River on his way home, and split his household in two before facing Esau. After Saul died, Ishbosheth ruled the northern tribes from Mahanaim while David held Hebron, and years later David fled there himself from Absalom and heard there that his son was dead.

malchiel.title: Malchiel
malchiel.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
malchiel.note: He was Asher's son, and his descendants made up one of the clans of Asher in the genealogies.

mamre.title: Mamre
mamre.note: Near Hebron, where Abraham settled and built an altar. The three visitors who told him Isaac was coming found him there. Mamre was also the name of an Amorite who stood with Abraham as an ally.

mamre-2.title: Mamre
mamre-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
mamre-2.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

manahath.title: Manahath
manahath.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
manahath.note: Shobal's son, Seir the Horite's grandson, and a clan chief of Edom in Genesis and Chronicles. The same name shows up in Benjamin's genealogy, probably for the related Manahathites, who are tied elsewhere to Zorah and Caleb's family.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

mash.title: Mash
mash.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
mash.note: The Table of Nations lists Mash as one of Aram's four sons. Chronicles gives the name as Meshech. Some connect his people with the Mount Masius range in what is now southeastern Turkey.

masrekah.title: Masrekah
masrekah.note: Samlah came from this town in Edom. He was one of the kings who ruled there before Israel had a king of its own.

massa.title: Massa
massa.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
massa.note: Ishmael had twelve sons, each the head of an Arabian tribe, and Massa was one. Assyrian records of the eighth century BC name a nomad tribe called Mas'a in the same region, and many scholars take them for his descendants.

matred.title: Matred
matred.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
matred.note: Mezahab's daughter, and the mother of Mehetabel, who married Hadar, the last king of Edom in the Genesis list. Women are rare in those lists, and nothing more is said of her.

medan.title: Medan
medan.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
medan.note: Abraham's son by Keturah, and the father of an Arabian tribe counted with Midian east of Canaan.

mehetabeel.title: Mehetabeel
mehetabeel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
mehetabeel.note: Wife of one of the early kings of Edom, in the king lists of Genesis and Chronicles.

mehujael.title: Mehujael
mehujael.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
mehujael.note: Irad's son and Methusael's father, in Cain's line on the way to Lamech.

melchizedek.title: Melchizedek
melchizedek.about: Priest living at the time of the Patriarchs
melchizedek.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High. He blessed Abraham and took a tenth of the spoils, and Genesis gives him no family, no birth and no death. Hebrews builds on that silence to explain how Jesus can be a priest without coming from Levi. Josephus reads the name as "the righteous king" and takes Salem for Jerusalem.

merari.title: Merari
merari.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
merari.note: Levi's third son. His descendants had the heavy parts of the tabernacle, the frames, bars, pillars and bases, which went by cart instead of being carried.

mesech-2.title: Mesech
mesech-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
mesech-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

mesha-4.title: Mesha
mesha-4.note: In the Table of Nations, Joktan's descendants settled from Mesha to Sephar. It was somewhere in Arabia, and exactly where is not known.

methusael.title: Methusael
methusael.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
methusael.note: Cain's line, father of Lamech and grandfather of Jabal, Jubal and Tubal-cain, the fathers of herders, musicians and metalworkers. The name looks like Methuselah, but Methuselah is in Seth's line and they are two men.

methuselah.title: Methuselah
methuselah.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
methuselah.note: Enoch's son and Noah's grandfather. Genesis gives him nine hundred sixty-nine years, longer than anyone else in the Bible. By the numbers in Genesis 5 he dies the year of the flood, though the text never connects the two. A Book of Noah fragment has him travel to find Enoch when his newborn grandson does not look human.

mezahab.title: Mezahab
mezahab.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
mezahab.note: Matred's father. His great claim is a granddaughter, Mehetabel, who married Hadar, the last king of Edom in the Genesis list.

mibsam.title: Mibsam
mibsam.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
mibsam.note: Ishmael's son, in the lists of Genesis and Chronicles.

mibzar.title: Mibzar
mibzar.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
mibzar.note: "Fortress." One of the chiefs of Edom from Esau's line, and like several names in that list it probably stands for a clan territory or stronghold as much as a man.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

midian-2.title: Midian
midian-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
midian-2.note: Abraham's son by Keturah, the man the Midianites traced themselves back to.

migdal-eder.title: Migdal-eder
migdal-eder.note: "Tower of the flock," near Bethlehem. Jacob pitched his tent there after burying Rachel by the road. Micah uses the name for Jerusalem's stronghold, promising its old rule would come back to the daughter of Zion.

milcah.title: Milcah
milcah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
milcah.note: Nahor's wife and Abraham's niece. Through her granddaughter Rebekah, who married Isaac, her branch of the family in Mesopotamia joined back into the main line.

mishma-2.title: Mishma
mishma-2.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
mishma-2.note: One of Ishmael's sons, from whom one of Ishmael's twelve tribes came, a set of twelve to match Israel's.

mizzah.title: Mizzah
mizzah.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
mizzah.note: A clan chief of Edom, from Esau's line, and the record has no more.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moab-2.title: Moab
moab-2.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

moreh.title: Moreh
moreh.note: The oak of Moreh, near Shechem, where Abraham stopped when he first came into Canaan, and Deuteronomy points back to it to show Israel where they would stand.

moriah.title: Moriah
moriah.note: Abraham was told to take Isaac to the land of Moriah and offer him there. Chronicles puts Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. Jewish tradition has long taken the two as the same ridge.

muppim.title: Muppim
muppim.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
muppim.note: Benjamin's son, one of Jacob's household who went down to Egypt. Numbers calls him Shupham, head of the Shuphamite clan.

naamah-2.title: Naamah
naamah-2.about: Woman living at the time before the Flood
naamah-2.note: Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.

naaman-4.title: Naaman
naaman-4.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
naaman-4.note: One of 4 men called Naaman. This one is a man from the wilderness years, named once in Genesis.

nahath.title: Nahath
nahath.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
nahath.note: An Edomite chief from Esau's line. The name was also carried by a Levite in Chronicles.

nahor.title: Nahor
nahor.about: Abraham's brother living at the time of the Patriarchs
nahor.note: Abraham's brother, Terah's son, who stayed in Mesopotamia when Abraham went to Canaan. His family there gave Isaac a wife, Rebekah, and gave Jacob his uncle and father-in-law, Laban.

nahor-2.title: Nahor
nahor-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
nahor-2.note: Terah's father, Abraham's grandfather, in the line from Shem. Joshua remembers that this family served other gods beyond the river.

naphish.title: Naphish
naphish.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphish.note: Ishmael's son. His people are among the tribes Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh beat in a war that Chronicles records.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

naptuhim.title: Naptuhim
naptuhim.note: One of the peoples descended from Mizraim, that is Egypt, in the Table of Nations. Some put them in Lower Egypt or the Nile Delta, but there is no agreement.

nebaioth.title: Nebaioth
nebaioth.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
nebaioth.note: Ishmael's firstborn. His descendants were an Arabian trading people, named next to Kedar in Isaiah.

nimrod.title: Nimrod
nimrod.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
nimrod.note: Noah's great-grandson through Ham, called a mighty hunter before the Lord. Genesis credits him with founding a run of Mesopotamian cities, Babel among them. Micah later uses his name for the land of Assyria itself.

nineveh.title: Nineveh
nineveh.note: The capital of the Assyrian empire. Jonah preached there against his will and watched the city repent, and Nahum later announced its destruction once it had gone back to its old cruelty.

noah.title: Noah
noah.about: Flood survivor living at the time before the Flood
noah.note: God picked him as the one righteous man of his generation and told him to build an ark. His family came through the flood with him, along with pairs of every kind of animal. Afterward God made a covenant with him.

nod.title: Nod
nod.note: It lay east of Eden, and Cain went there after he killed Abel. Nod means wandering, which fits the sentence God had just passed on him.

obal.title: Obal
obal.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
obal.note: First Chronicles spells him Ebal, but in Genesis 10:28 he is Obal, one of the thirteen sons of Joktan.

ohad.title: Ohad
ohad.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ohad.note: The third son of Simeon, one of Jacob's family who went down into Egypt. He is missing from the Simeonite clan lists in Numbers 26, so his line may have died out or been folded into another clan.

omar.title: Omar
omar.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
omar.note: Esau's grandson and an Edomite clan chief, listed in the genealogies of Genesis 36.

on.title: On
on.note: Joseph's wife Asenath was the daughter of Potipherah, priest of On. The city stood on the east bank of the Nile near modern Cairo and was the center of Egyptian sun worship, which is why the Greeks called it Heliopolis.

onam-2.title: Onam
onam-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
onam-2.note: A Horite clan name in Edom's genealogies, listed in Genesis 36:23 and again in 1 Chronicles 1:40.

onan.title: Onan
onan.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
onan.note: Judah's second son. Custom required him to father a child for his dead brother through the widow Tamar. He made sure it never happened, and God put him to death for it.

ophir-2.title: Ophir
ophir-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
ophir-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

padan.title: Padan
padan.note: Short for Paddan-aram, the country around Haran in upper Mesopotamia where Abraham's brother Nahor settled. Rebekah came from there. Jacob ran there years later to get away from Esau.

pai.title: Pai
pai.note: Hadar, last of Edom's early kings in the Genesis list, ruled from Pai, also spelled Pau, and nobody knows where in Edom it stood.

pallu.title: Pallu
pallu.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
pallu.note: Reuben's son. His descendants, the Palluites, were one of the clans counted in the wilderness.

paran.title: Paran
paran.note: Ishmael grew up in this wilderness after Hagar was sent away with him, and Israel camped there for part of the long march.

pathrusim.title: Pathrusim
pathrusim.note: Descendants of Mizraim, named after Pathros, the country along the Nile south of Memphis.

peleg.title: Peleg
peleg.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
peleg.note: In his days the earth was divided, Genesis says. That is usually taken to mean the scattering at Babel. He came down from Shem.

peniel.title: Peniel
peniel.note: Jacob wrestled here through the night by the Jabbok River. He came away with a new name, Israel, and a limp he kept. He called the place Peniel, face of God, because he had seen God face to face and lived.

perez.title: Perez
perez.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
