perez.note: Judah's son by Tamar. He pushed out ahead of his twin Zerah, though Zerah's hand had already been marked with a scarlet thread as the firstborn. His line runs through Boaz to David.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

pharaoh-2.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-2.note: Joseph's Pharaoh. Potiphar was his officer, his baker and butler landed in prison with Joseph, and his dreams of fat and thin cows were what got Joseph out and set him over Egypt.

pharaoh-6.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-6.note: Abraham went down to Egypt in a famine and passed his wife off as his sister, and this Pharaoh took her into his house. God struck the household with plagues. Pharaoh sent them both away.

phichol.title: Phichol
phichol.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
phichol.note: He commanded Abimelech's army, and was there when Abimelech made peace with Abraham, and again a generation later with Isaac.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phut-2.title: Phut
phut-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
phut-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

phuvah.title: Phuvah
phuvah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phuvah.note: Issachar's son, usually spelled Puvah, in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.

pildash.title: Pildash
pildash.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
pildash.note: Nahor, Abraham's brother, had eight sons by Milcah, and Pildash was one.

pinon.title: Pinon
pinon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
pinon.note: An Edomite chief in Genesis 36:41 and 1 Chronicles 1:52, whom many scholars take to be the same name as Punon.

pison.title: Pison
pison.note: One of four rivers that branch from the river watering Eden, said to wind around the land of Havilah, where there is gold, bdellium and onyx. Nobody has ever pinned it on a map.

poti-pherah.title: Poti-pherah
poti-pherah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
poti-pherah.note: Priest of On. His daughter Asenath married Joseph after Pharaoh raised Joseph up, so Ephraim and Manasseh were his grandsons.

potiphar.title: Potiphar
potiphar.about: Egyptian living at the time of the Patriarchs
potiphar.note: An Egyptian official. He bought Joseph as a slave and soon had him running the whole household. When Potiphar's wife accused Joseph falsely, Potiphar had him put in prison.

raamah.title: Raamah
raamah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
raamah.note: His sons Sheba and Dedan fathered Arabian trading peoples. Raamah himself was a son of Cush, and Ezekiel lists Raamah's merchants among those who brought Tyre its spices and precious stones.

raamses.title: Raamses
raamses.note: The Israelites built Raamses, also spelled Rameses, as a store city for Pharaoh in the eastern Nile Delta, alongside Pithom. When they left Egypt, this is where they set out from.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

raguel.title: Raguel
raguel.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
raguel.note: In Genesis 36 he is an Edomite chief. The record elsewhere ties the name to Jethro, Moses's father-in-law, the Midianite priest, but these verses are the Edomite.

rebekah.title: Rebekah
rebekah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rebekah.note: Abraham's servant went back to Mesopotamia to find Isaac a wife. He asked for water, and Rebekah offered to water his camels too. That was the sign he had been waiting for.

rehoboth.title: Rehoboth
rehoboth.note: It means broad places, and the name turns up in more than one spot. Genesis 10:11 puts a Rehoboth among the cities built in Assyria, and an Edomite king came from a Rehoboth by the river.

rehoboth-2.title: Rehoboth
rehoboth-2.note: Named once, in Genesis, and nowhere else.

resen.title: Resen
resen.note: Between Nineveh and Calah, among the cities Nimrod is said to have built in Assyria. Some read the verse to mean the settlements grew into one great city.

reu.title: Reu
reu.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
reu.note: Between Noah's family and Abraham the genealogy runs through Reu, a descendant of Shem.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

reumah.title: Reumah
reumah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
reumah.note: She was the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and bore him four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.

riphath.title: Riphath
riphath.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
riphath.note: Gomer's second son and Japheth's grandson. Ancient readers tied his descendants to peoples of northern Asia Minor, possibly the Paphlagonians, though nobody can be sure.

rosh.title: Rosh
rosh.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
rosh.note: Genesis 46:21 lists him among the sons of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob. He is missing from the longer lists of Benjamin's line in Numbers 26 and 1 Chronicles 7 and 8.

sabta.title: Sabta
sabta.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sabta.note: A son of Cush and grandson of Ham, also spelled Sabtah, and ancestor of a people among the early tribes of Arabia or northeast Africa.

sabtecha.title: Sabtecha
sabtecha.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sabtecha.note: Cush's fifth son, listed with Seba, Havilah, Sabtah and Raamah in the table of nations. Like his brothers' names, his almost certainly stands for a people.

salah.title: Salah
salah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
salah.note: Son of Arphaxad and father of Eber. He is a link in the chain from Noah to Abraham.

salem.title: Salem
salem.note: The old name for Jerusalem. Melchizedek was its king when he came out to bless Abraham, and Psalm 76 uses the name again for the city where God lives.

samlah.title: Samlah
samlah.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
samlah.note: Edom had kings before Israel did, and Samlah was one of them.

sarah-2.title: Sarah
sarah-2.about: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sarah-2.note: Not Abraham's wife but a different woman, named in the family lists at Genesis 46:17, Numbers 26:46 and 1 Chronicles 7:30, from the years in Egypt and the wilderness.

sarah.title: Sarah
sarah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
sarah.note: Abraham's wife. She was ninety when Isaac was born, after decades of being unable to have children, and earlier she had doubted the promise could come through her at all.

sarai.title: Sarai
sarai.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
sarai.note: It was what Sarah was called before Genesis 17, when God changed her name as part of the covenant and promised that she would be the mother of nations and kings.

seba.title: Seba
seba.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
seba.note: Son of Cush, whose descendants the Psalms put with Sheba, a far kingdom in Africa or Arabia bringing tribute to Israel's king.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

seir-2.title: Seir
seir-2.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
seir-2.note: Seir the Horite, whose sons are listed in Genesis 36:20 and again in 1 Chronicles 1:38. They were the people in the land before Esau's line took it.

sephar.title: Sephar
sephar.note: Joktan's descendants settled as far east as Sephar, with Mesha marking the other end (Genesis 10:30). It is commonly identified with Zafar on the southern Arabian coast.

sered.title: Sered
sered.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sered.note: Zebulun's son, who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family and from whom the Seredites came.

serug.title: Serug
serug.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
serug.note: Abraham's great-grandfather, a descendant of Shem, on the line that joins Noah's family to the patriarchs.

seth.title: Seth
seth.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
seth.note: After Cain killed Abel, Eve had a third son. She named him Seth, saying God had given her another child in Abel's place. His line is the one Genesis follows forward.

shammah.title: Shammah
shammah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shammah.note: Genesis 36 has a Shammah among its chiefs, and 1 Samuel 16:9 and 17:13 name one as a brother of David. The name was used more than once.

shaul.title: Shaul
shaul.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
shaul.note: A king from the patriarchs. Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him 4 times.

shaul-2.title: Shaul
shaul-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shaul-2.note: Genesis and 3 other books name him 4 times, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

shaveh.title: Shaveh
shaveh.note: The king of Sodom came out to meet Abram in the Valley of Shaveh. Abram had just rescued Lot and beaten the eastern kings. It was also called the King's Valley.

shaveh-kiriathaim.title: Shaveh Kiriathaim
shaveh-kiriathaim.note: The plain around Kiriathaim, east of the Jordan. The eastern kings beat the Emim there in Genesis 14:5.

sheba-3.title: Sheba
sheba-3.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sheba-3.note: A name among the nations in Genesis 10:7 and 1 Chronicles 1:9. Job 1:15 has raiders from Sheba carrying off Job's oxen and killing his servants.

sheba-4.title: Sheba
sheba-4.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sheba-4.note: One of 4 men called Sheba. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

sheba-5.title: Sheba
sheba-5.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sheba-5.note: A man from the patriarchs, named twice across Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

shebah.title: Shebah
shebah.note: Not a person but a well. Isaac's servants dug it, and Genesis 26:33 says it gave Beersheba its name, the well of the oath, or of seven.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

shechem-2.title: Shechem
shechem-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shechem-2.note: The Canaanite prince who raped Jacob's daughter Dinah. Her brothers Simeon and Levi answered it with a massacre.

shelah.title: Shelah
shelah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shelah.note: Judah's third son by his Canaanite wife. Judah held him back from marrying Tamar, the widow, as custom said he should. That broken promise is what drove Tamar to disguise herself.

sheleph.title: Sheleph
sheleph.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sheleph.note: Son of Joktan, and the ancestor of one of the many Joktanite peoples who settled the Arabian peninsula.

shem.title: Shem
shem.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shem.note: Noah's oldest son. The Semitic peoples, Abraham's line among them, all trace back to him, and Genesis 10 follows his descendants down to Eber.

shemeber.title: Shemeber
shemeber.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
shemeber.note: King of Zeboiim, one of the five cities of the plain. He rebelled against Chedorlaomer with the others, and that is what brought the invasion of Genesis 14.

shephi.title: Shephi
shephi.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
shephi.note: Son of Shobal, of the line of Seir the Horite, among Edom's clan chiefs, and Genesis 36:23 spells him Shepho.

shillem.title: Shillem
shillem.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shillem.note: Son of Naphtali. He went down to Egypt with Jacob, and his clan was counted again in the wilderness. Chronicles calls him Shallum.

shiloh-2.title: Shiloh
shiloh-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shiloh-2.note: Jacob's blessing on Judah says the sceptre stays "until Shiloh comes," and nobody has ever agreed what that means. Some read Shiloh as a title for a coming ruler from Judah.

shimron.title: Shimron
shimron.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shimron.note: A son of Issachar, and the Shimronites took their name from him.

shinab.title: Shinab
shinab.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
shinab.note: Admah was one of the five cities of the plain, with Sodom and Gomorrah, and Shinab was its king when Chedorlaomer came. He was one of the kings who rebelled.

shinar.title: Shinar
shinar.note: The old name for the land of Babylon. The tower of Babel went up there, and much later it was the heart of Nebuchadnezzar's empire.

shobal.title: Shobal
shobal.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
shobal.note: An Edomite clan chief, descended from Seir. The name was used again for a man of Judah.

shua.title: Shua
shua.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shua.note: A Canaanite. Judah married his daughter, and she bore Er, Onan and Shelah.

shuah.title: Shuah
shuah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
shuah.note: One of the sons Abraham had by Keturah. His people settled in Arabia, and Job's friend Bildad the Shuhite probably came from them.

shuni.title: Shuni
shuni.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
shuni.note: Gad's son, who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family and from whom the Shunites came.

shur.title: Shur
shur.note: The wilderness on Egypt's northeastern frontier, between Egypt and Philistia. The name probably comes from a wall the Egyptians built there against raiders. Hagar ran toward it when Sarah sent her away.

siddim.title: Siddim
siddim.note: A valley full of tar pits. The kings of Sodom, Gomorrah and three other cities fought Chedorlaomer's invading coalition there, and some of them fell into the pits.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sidon-2.title: Sidon
sidon-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
sidon-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

sinite.title: Sinite
sinite.note: A Canaanite clan on the Phoenician coast, in the Table of Nations. The city is generally placed near Arka, though no one is certain.

sitnah.title: Sitnah
sitnah.note: The second well Isaac's herdsmen dug in the valley of Gerar. The Philistines there fought over it as they had over the first, so it was called hostility.

sodom.title: Sodom
sodom.note: Sodom was destroyed by fire from heaven along with Gomorrah, and the rest of Scripture keeps pointing back to it as the picture of judgment. It was one of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

syrian-2.title: Syrian
syrian-2.note: In Genesis the word marks the family in Paddan-aram as Arameans, and Deuteronomy 26:5 uses it once more.

tamar-2.title: Tamar
tamar-2.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
tamar-2.note: Judah's daughter-in-law, widowed twice with no heir. Judah held back his third son, so she dressed as a prostitute and conceived twins by Judah himself. He ended up saying she was more righteous than he was, and Ruth 4:12 blesses a family in her name.

tarah.title: Tarah
tarah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tarah.note: Abraham's father, whose family line Genesis 11 traces. Joshua 24:2 names him again.

tarshish-4.title: Tarshish
tarshish-4.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tarshish-4.note: Genesis names him once, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

tebah.title: Tebah
tebah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tebah.note: Nahor's son by his concubine Reumah, and the first one named. Nahor was Abraham's brother.

tema-2.title: Tema
tema-2.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
tema-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

temani.title: Temani
temani.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
temani.note: Teman was Esau's grandson, and his Edomite clan had a name for wisdom. This is the word for that clan, and it is what Eliphaz is called all through Job.

thahash.title: Thahash
thahash.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
thahash.note: Another of Nahor's sons by Reumah, listed once in Genesis 22:24.

tidal.title: Tidal
tidal.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
tidal.note: King of Goyim, one of the four eastern kings under Chedorlaomer who attacked a group of Canaanite cities and carried off Lot. Abraham went after them and beat them. His name matches Tudhaliya, a name several Hittite kings carried.

timna.title: Timna
timna.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
timna.note: Two Edomites. One was a concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, and her son Amalek fathered the people who were Israel's enemies for generations. The other was an Edomite clan chief.

tiras.title: Tiras
tiras.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tiras.note: Japheth's youngest son in the Table of Nations. Genesis does not say where his people lived. Josephus connected them with the Thracians, and nobody can confirm it.

togarmah.title: Togarmah
togarmah.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
togarmah.note: Gomer's son and Japheth's grandson. Ezekiel's people of Togarmah trade horses and mules, from somewhere in eastern Asia Minor.

tola.title: Tola
tola.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
tola.note: Here the verses are the man from the family lists, not the judge. He is in Genesis 46:13 among those who went down to Egypt, and in the Numbers 26 census and 1 Chronicles 7.

tubal-2.title: Tubal
tubal-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tubal-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

tubal-cain.title: Tubal-cain
tubal-cain.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
tubal-cain.note: Lamech's son by Zillah, in Cain's line, and the first metalworker the Bible names, forging tools of bronze and iron. His half-brother Jabal fathered the herdsmen and Jubal the musicians.

ur.title: Ur
ur.note: Abraham's family started out from here, Terah leading them toward Canaan. Ur was a big Sumerian city near the mouth of the Euphrates. Leonard Woolley dug it in the 1920s and 1930s and found a royal cemetery full of gold.

uz-3.title: Uz
uz-3.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
uz-3.note: One of 4 men called Uz. This one is a man from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

uz-2.title: Uz
uz-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
uz-2.note: Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

uz-4.title: Uz
uz-4.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
uz-4.note: A man from the patriarchs, and Genesis is the only book that names him.

uzal.title: Uzal
uzal.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
uzal.note: Joktan's son, and tradition ties the name to an old city in Yemen.

zaavan.title: Zaavan
zaavan.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
zaavan.note: An Edomite chief descended from Seir the Horite, also spelled Zavan.

zaphnath-paaneah.title: Zaphnath-paaneah
zaphnath-paaneah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zaphnath-paaneah.note: The Egyptian name Pharaoh gave Joseph when he made him governor over Egypt, and what it means is disputed.

zarah.title: Zarah
zarah.about: Judah's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zarah.note: Judah's son by Tamar, Perez's twin. His hand came out first and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on it, and then Perez was born ahead of him.

zarah-4.title: Zarah
zarah-4.about: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
zarah-4.note: One of 6 men called Zarah. This one is a king from the patriarchs, named twice in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

zarah-2.title: Zarah
zarah-2.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zarah-2.note: Not Judah's son. This Zerah is in the Genesis 36 family lists and in 1 Chronicles 1:37, one of the Idumaean names.

zeboiim.title: Zeboiim
zeboiim.note: One of the five cities of the plain, with Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Bela, destroyed with Sodom. In Hosea 11:8 God says he cannot make Israel like Admah and Zeboiim.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zemarite.title: Zemarite
zemarite.note: A Canaanite people named for Zemar, a Phoenician coastal town under the Lebanon range. The Amarna letters call it Sumur.

zephi.title: Zephi
zephi.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
zephi.note: Eliphaz's son and Esau's grandson, one of the clan chiefs of Edom. Nothing more is recorded.

zerah.title: Zerah
zerah.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zerah.note: Genesis and Exodus name him twice, and he is a man from the wilderness years.

zibeon.title: Zibeon
zibeon.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
zibeon.note: A Horite chief in the Edom lists of Genesis 36, and Esau's wife Oholibamah came from his line.

zillah.title: Zillah
zillah.about: Woman living at the time before the Flood
zillah.note: Lamech's second wife, in Cain's line, and mother of Tubal-cain, who forged tools of bronze and iron.

zilpah.title: Zilpah
zilpah.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
zilpah.note: Leah's servant. In the contest between Leah and Rachel for sons she was given to Jacob, and she bore him Gad and Asher.

zimran.title: Zimran
zimran.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zimran.note: Abraham's son by Keturah. He is generally taken as the father of an Arabian tribe that nobody can now identify.

ziphion.title: Ziphion
ziphion.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ziphion.note: Gad's son, one of the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob. Numbers 26:15 calls him Zephon.

zoar.title: Zoar
zoar.note: Lot asked that this little town be spared so he could run to it, and it was, while Sodom and Gomorrah burned. It was first called Bela, and it lay where Moab met the Dead Sea plain.

zohar.title: Zohar
zohar.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
zohar.note: Two men. One was Ephron's father, the Hittite who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah. The other is a son of Simeon in the family lists.

zuzims.title: Zuzims
zuzims.note: A people east of the Jordan whom Chedorlaomer's coalition beat on the campaign that ended with Lot carried off from Sodom. Some think they are the Zamzummim.
